data.description:
Discovered while proving the MCP OOM root cause on witted-invisible-roan (9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496). Shares that bug's root cause — whole-store materialization — but is a DIFFERENT and worse retention profile, and its contribution was NOT separately measured, so it is filed rather than folded into that fix.

## Observed

`build_plan_relation_snapshot` calls `reduce_all_tickets` with all three filters OFF — the MAXIMAL compile, including verbose `session_log` and `code_review` bodies:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py:257-262` — `exclude_archived=False, exclude_deleted=False, exclude_session_logs=False`.
- The result is fanned into `states: dict[str, dict]` (`relation_snapshot.py:268`) and returned as `PlanRelationSnapshot.ticket_states_by_id` (frozen dataclass field, `relation_snapshot.py:65`).
- That snapshot is held by `PlanReviewGeneration.relation_snapshot` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:48`) and threaded through the whole multi-pass review, captured by the fan-out closures (`plan_review/pass1.py:434`, `plan_review/container_stage.py:259`, `plan_review/generation.py:154`).

## Why this is worse than the read-path case

On the read path the whole-store compile is a TRANSIENT — measured 243.4 MB on this store (8,879 tickets), released as soon as the call returns. Here it is **retained for the full duration of a plan review**, which `AGENTS.md` documents as 15-20 minutes. Concurrent reviews therefore stack: N overlapping reviews hold N copies simultaneously, and on the 7.6 GiB box the MCP container shares the host with Gerrit, the review-bot and opcert.

Measured on the real store for the equivalent compile: 243.4 MB per snapshot held. Ten to nineteen overlapping reviews reproduces the reported 368 MiB -> 4.5-4.8 GiB curve on its own, which is consistent with the reported busy window ("six changes under review, several agents pushing patchsets").

## Why it is not fixed by the 9ea3 change

The fix landing on 9ea3 adds an `omit_fields` projection applied INSIDE `reduce_all_tickets`' per-ticket loop, and uses it from `list_states` and `find_ready_tickets`. It deliberately does NOT touch this call site: unlike the discovery reads, the plan reviewer may genuinely consume the bodies and signature material of related tickets, so which fields (if any) are droppable here needs its own analysis and its own measurement.

## Suggested direction (not yet validated)

`relation_snapshot.py:505-589` and `plan_review/__init__.py:489-490` appear to read only the subject, its children and its prerequisites out of `ticket_states_by_id`. If that holds, the snapshot could retain full states for just the pinned subset and lean states (or nothing) for the rest, which is the same shape as the two-pass `find_ready_tickets` fix. That reading needs to be confirmed against every consumer before it is acted on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: every consumer of `PlanRelationSnapshot.ticket_states_by_id` is enumerated with citations, and the set of fields each actually reads is recorded.
- [ ] AC2: peak and retained memory of a plan-review generation is measured on a real-sized store, before and after, under comparable load — the contribution of THIS site is established separately rather than bundled with the 9ea3 read-path fix.
- [ ] AC3: a held-out regression test asserts the retained snapshot does not scale with whole-store size, verified RED before the fix and RED again when the fix is perturbed.
- [ ] AC4: `rebar review-plan` verdicts are unchanged — a fixture review produces byte-identical findings before and after.

## Explicitly out of scope

A container memory limit, a concurrency cap on reviews, or a periodic restart. Those change which process the kernel kills; they do not reduce what is retained. Same standing decision as 9ea3 and ADRs 0079 / 0104.
data.title: Plan-review holds a maximal whole-store compile for the entire 15-20 minute review
